# Evidence and Evolution Principles {.unnumbered}

An operating agentic system generates trajectories, not isolated predictions. Evaluation and observability must therefore capture temporal behavior, state transitions, tool effects, and recovery decisions, then connect those records to controlled system improvement.

::: {#pri-trajectory-evidence .callout-principle title="Evaluate the trajectory and its outcome"}

**Invariant**: End-state quality alone cannot reveal unsafe actions, wasted work, hidden intervention, or brittle recovery along the path.

**Implication**: Evaluation suites need outcome, process, resource, safety, and intervention measures at the level where each claim is made.

:::

::: {#pri-replay-envelope .callout-principle title="Replay has an envelope"}

**Invariant**: Exact replay requires control over every relevant source of nondeterminism; otherwise replay reconstructs evidence rather than reproducing execution.

**Implication**: Traces must record model versions, prompts, state snapshots, tool responses, policy decisions, and environment identifiers, while clearly stating what cannot be reproduced.

:::

::: {#pri-controlled-improvement .callout-principle title="Improvement requires comparison"}

**Invariant**: A production change is evidence of improvement only when it is evaluated against a stable baseline under representative conditions.

**Implication**: Deployment, monitoring, incident review, and regression testing must form one versioned feedback loop.

:::
